title: Sustained Deep-Network Binding Is a Correlate of Accessibility Concept Emergence: Evidence from the Pythia and GPT-2 Model Suites
abstract: Sustained deep-network binding of accessibility compounds appears to be a necessary structural condition for behavioral capability-present in every model that correctly defines core concepts, absent in every model that fails. We use Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) as our test domain because accessibility represents a specialized, low-frequency domain in webscale training data-a small, well-defined vocabulary with unambiguous answers and direct relevance to real-world tooling decisions, making it an unusually clean lens for studying emergence: concepts are concrete enough to evaluate and rare enough to show scale sensitivity. Using the Pythia suite (160M-6.9B) and GPT-2 (small-XL) with TransformerLens, we investigate not just what models know but how that knowledge is encoded internally. All models show compound binding in early layers; the differentiating factor is whether that binding persists to late network layers. Screen reader, skip link, and alt text emerge behaviorally at ~2.8B; WCAG first appears at 6.9B; Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) exhibits fluent wrongness at every scale tested-producing confident, plausible expansions that are consistently incorrect. Models prefer correct definitions before they can produce them, and a declarative-evaluative gap persists even at maximum scale: models that correctly define accessibility concepts cannot reliably identify violations in code.

title: Quantum information processing and communication protocols based on time-bin entangled photonic qudits
abstract: Encoding quantum information into time-bin entangled photons offers a physics-rich framework for both fundamental and applied quantum science. Here, we present two frameworks enabling the generation and manipulation of time-bin entangled photonic qudits for both fundamental and applied quantum information processing. The first framework consists of a scalable synthetic temporal photonic lattice implemented on a coupled fiber-loop system that is employed to explore and dynamically control the evolution of the discrete-time quantum walk of time-bin entangled photon states. The other framework consists of a modular, fiber-pigtailed, integrated photonic platform enabling the generation and processing of time-bin entangled qudits that were used to demonstrate the first Bennett-Brassard-Mermin 1992 QKD protocol extended to qudits. We operate the entangled qudits at processing speeds typical of standard telecommunication systems at 10s of GBaud.

title: On Representation Error in Quantum Option Pricing: A Diagnostic Study of the Standard Qiskit Implementation
abstract: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) is an attractive financial derivative pricing algorithm with the potential for a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo approaches. Yet, quantum advantage will only be found if not just fault-tolerant hardware but also an accurate representation of the financial problem on a quantum circuit is achieved. This paper offers a reproducible, diagnostic examination of the default Qiskit Finance application to European option pricing. We present a critical diagnostic marker: the classical discretized price, which is the classically computed expected payoff on the quantum model's actual grid. Our convergence analysis of low-qubit models (4, 5, and 6 uncertainty qubits) shows that for this particular configuration, representation error, which arises due to imprecise trigonometric encoding of the option payoff function, is the prevalent source of error, much larger compared to the discretization error. In a 6-qubit model, the representation error was 0.17699 USD, which is an order of magnitude larger than the discretization error of -0.01200 USD. We illustrate how a different Piecewise Linear (PWL) encoding can successfully remove this representation error, but at the expense of more circuit resources. Our results, for the vanilla, low-qubit Qiskit Finance circuits we used, indicate that the creation of high-fidelity, resource-conscious problem encodings is a pressing and essential problem on the road to applicable quantum advantage in finance.
